$comment: Performance budgets (warden-plan.md, Performance), approved by the user. null = PLACEHOLDER, not set yet: the number is measured and reported but nothing fails. "measured" notes what each budget was based on.

coreIdleMemoryMB.what: server private memory after 5 s idle, with its session table full (200 sessions)
coreIdleMemoryMB.measured: step 4.1: measured 1.7 MB with no accounts; room for accounts, readings and capped history; step 4.3: 2.0 MB with 200 sessions

coreIdleCpuPercent.what: server CPU over 20 s idle, with its session table full

windowMemoryMB.what: desktop app with the window open: the app and its WebView2 processes, private memory after the page loaded and sat idle
windowMemoryMB.measured: step 4.4: measured 172 to 181 MB (the app and its WebView2 processes, Overview with no accounts); room for accounts and the sessions table

desktopTrayMemoryMB.what: desktop app in the tray after its window was opened and closed: private memory after 5 s idle
desktopTrayMemoryMB.measured: step 4.4: measured 7.4 MB after the window was closed (4.3 MB started in the tray); the same budget as the core alone

desktopTrayCpuPercent.what: desktop app in the tray after its window was opened and closed: CPU over 20 s idle
desktopTrayCpuPercent.measured: step 4.4: measured 0.00% over 5 s idle; the same budget as the core alone

routeHookMs.what: median time of `warden route` while nothing changed (prints nothing), the routing hook on every message
routeHookMs.measured: step 4.2: measured 6.3 ms with three accounts

routeHookPrintMs.what: median time of `warden route` when it prints the guidance (a session's first message, or a change)
routeHookPrintMs.measured: step 4.2: measured 6.9 ms with three accounts

statusHookMs.what: median time of one status hook event (`warden event`: started, the event read, sent over the pipe and answered), when run without async
statusHookMs.measured: step 4.3: measured 9.9 ms with curl; the pipe run: 5.3 ms for `warden event`

statusEventCpuMs.what: server CPU time per status hook event with four windows waiting for changes (each answered) and three accounts with hook files
statusEventCpuMs.measured: measured 1.33 to 1.42 ms before the hook state was kept in memory, 0.38 to 0.80 ms after (three runs of 1000 events each)

statusHookDownMs.what: median time of one status hook event (`warden event`) with Warden stopped
statusHookDownMs.measured: step 4.3: measured 9.4 ms with curl; the pipe run: 5.4 ms for `warden event`, which finds no pipe

cliBinaryKB.measured: step 4.2: measured 1057 KB (with the usage endpoint's TLS for the background refresh)

desktopBinaryKB.what: release warden-desktop.exe (the installer adds the UI files and warden.exe)
